note: How the red and green lines' stations are laid out, for tools/build-stations.ts (see there for the format). Each is read from Albert Guillaumes' drawing of the station (estacions.albertguillaumes.cat, used as a reference only), with its exits at OpenStreetMap's subway entrances. T-Centralen, Odenplan and Fridhemsplan aren't here: they are his 3D models (public/data/stations.json).

Östermalmstorg.note: Two platform halls, one for each track, joined at both ends and in the middle. From the south-west end, escalators climb in two flights to a long ticket hall under Stureplan with four exits; from the north-east end, two flights to the hall at Sibyllegatan and Nybrogatan.

Gamla stan.note: Two island platforms at ground level, a metre or two above the streets beside them, red on the inner side of each and green on the outer. Stairs go down through each platform to the ticket hall under the tracks, and up from it to the streets.

Slussen.note: Two curved island platforms in one hall, decked over: from west to east the green line's northbound track, the red line's, a wall between the red line's two tracks with Bengt Rafael Sundberg's blue screens in its openings, the red line's southbound track and the green line's; each line's trains stop at the same island going the same way, the red on its inner side. Two flights of stairs from each platform, rising towards each other, and two lifts between them climb to the ticket hall at street level under Stockholms sjömanshem, with gates at each end: north to the doors on Ryssgården, south to the doors on Katarinavägen. From the platforms' south ends escalators climb to a passage across over the tracks (Sune Fogde's wall), three more up to the hall at Götgatan and its gates, and a last flight to its door on Götgatan. From OpenStreetMap's indoor ways (2026: the stairs, lifts, gates and doors), the laser scan (Ryssgården 12.85 m, Götgatan 29.0 m) and photographs; the ticket hall's floor (12.9 m) and the heights of the passages to Götgatan are guessed.

Mariatorget.note: Two platform halls, one for each track, the platforms within, either side of a core of rock about 9 m wide that stops short of their ends, joined round its ends and by a passage a little east of its middle (Albert Guillaumes's drawing; OpenStreetMap's platforms). From the western end three escalators and an inclined lift climb west-south-west to a ticket hall at street level under the courtyards, and on to the doors at Torkel Knutssonsgatan 33; from the eastern end three escalators and an inclined lift climb east-north-east to a hall under Wollmar Yxkullsgatan, from which two flights of stairs climb to the doors at the corner of Swedenborgsgatan, and a lift to its glass house on Wollmar Yxkullsgatan's pavement (OpenStreetMap's indoor ways; the lift house's height from Lantmäteriet's laser scan; the eastern hall's depth inferred from its stairs and the escalators' length).

Zinkensdamm.note: Two straight platform halls, one for each track, the tracks on the outside and the side platforms within, either side of a core of rock 9 m wide, joined a little west of the middle (Albert Guillaumes's drawing; OpenStreetMap's platforms). East of the join three escalators and an inclined lift climb east inside the core, behind glass screens at their foot, to the ticket hall under Brännkyrkagatan; a passage runs on east under the street to a cross passage under Ringvägen's pavement, with stairs south up into the entrance pavilion at Ringvägen 8 and a lift north to its glass house on the pavement (OpenStreetMap's indoor ways; the pavilion's and the lift house's outlines and heights from Lantmäteriet's laser scan; the ticket hall's depth inferred from the stairs into the pavilion).

Hornstull.note: Two straight platform halls, one for each track, the tracks on the outside and the side platforms within, either side of a core of rock 11.5 m wide in two lengths, joined round its ends and by a passage between its lengths (Albert Guillaumes's drawing; OpenStreetMap's platforms). From the western end two escalators, stairs and an inclined lift climb west to a hall under Hornsbruksgatan, past the gates and along a passage lined with shops to the doors in the buildings round Hornstull: stairs and an escalator north to Långholmsgatan, stairs south to Hornsgatan, and a passage west to stairs up to Bergsunds strand under a building's arcade. From the eastern end three escalators and an inclined lift climb east to a hall at street level in the building on Hornsbruksgatan's northern side, by Högalidsparken (OpenStreetMap's indoor ways, 2026, with the gates, shops and lifts; the western hall's depth from its stairs to the streets, the eastern escalators' rise from the street).

Liljeholmen.note: Three platforms side by side in a hall under the deck of Liljeholmstorget, from west to east an island between the two tracks of the line, an island between its third track (where trains turning back stand, on Albert Guillaumes's drawing) and the eastern track, and a platform beyond the eastern track, behind it the glass wall of the bus terminal. At the south end each platform has stairs and an escalator side by side climbing to the 1964 hall on the square, its gates and a passage across it, with doors onto the square to the east and down to Liljeholmsgränd to the west, and a glazed walkway south along Liljeholmsgränd to the inclined lift up Nybohovsberget. At the north end stairs and escalators climb from each platform into the hall in the ground floor of the buildings on the deck, joined by a bridge over the tracks, with doors onto the square and the street. From OpenStreetMap's indoor ways (2026: the flights, the landings, the gates, the doors, the walkway), the laser scan (the deck and the square 5.0 to 5.2 m over the platforms, Liljeholmsgränd 0.5 m under them) and photographs.

Karlaplan.note: An island platform deep in the rock. Escalators climb from each end of it to a ticket hall: Valhallavägen to the north-east, Karlaplan to the south-west.

Gärdet.note: Two platform halls, one for each track, the platforms within, either side of a core of rock about 10 m wide, joined through it at both ends and by a passage in the middle (OpenStreetMap's indoor ways, Albert Guillaumes's drawing). From the south-west end three escalators and an inclined lift climb to the ticket hall at Askrikegatan's sunken court, with a lift up to Brantingsgatan; from the north-east end three escalators and an inclined lift climb about 17 m (inferred from OpenStreetMap's lengths against the south-west's) to a hall in the rock, with lifts up to Furusundsgatan and a long passage falling to Tegeluddsvägen.

Ropsten.note: The line's northern end, high over Ropsten's bus square: two viaducts, each with one track and a platform on the side towards the other, an open gap between them. At the south-west end the two platforms are joined in a covered concourse. From its end escalators and stairs go down in the gap to the ticket hall on the ground beneath, a crossbridge with a lift crosses the gap halfway along, and another at the north-east end leads to the glazed hall over Lidingöbanan's stop, where escalators and stairs go down to the trams. The platforms' railings and roofs are drawn by src/detail/ropsten-station.ts. Positions from OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping and Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2021).

Stadion.note: An island platform, its rock left standing in two long pillars down the middle. From the north end a long flight climbs to a ticket hall under Valhallavägen with exits to both sides of it and to the Stadion; from the south end, escalators climb to Karlavägen.

Tekniska högskolan.note: An island platform 157 m long and 27 m wide round two cores of rock, a passage between them (Albert Guillaumes' drawing, its scale read off Roslagsbanan's platforms beside it). From a lobby 10 m wide at each end of the platform three escalators and an inclined lift climb (OpenStreetMap's indoor ways): at the north-west about 14.5 m, to a hall under Valhallavägen with stairs and a lift up to it and a passage to Odengatan; at the south-east about 13 m, to a hall under the bus terminal with escalators, stairs and a lift up to Valhallavägen, a passage to Stockholms östra and one to Danderydsgatan.

Universitetet.note: An island platform 156 m long and 31.6 m wide round two cores of rock, a passage between them 21 m north of its middle (Albert Guillaumes' drawing). From a lobby at its south end four escalators and an inclined lift climb about 21 m to the south-south-east (OpenStreetMap's indoor ways) to the ticket hall in the sunken building by the square at Frescati.

Bergshamra.note: An island platform 177 m long and 28 m wide round two cores of rock, a passage between them about 40 m north of its middle (Albert Guillaumes' drawing; OpenStreetMap's indoor ways). From a notch in the northern core's end by the passage three escalators climb 14 m through the core to the northern ticket hall, from which an escalator and stairs climb to the pavilion on Bergshamra torg and a lift to the courtyard beside it; two lifts climb to the hall from the platform's northern end. From its southern end a passage on the level runs under Bergshamravägen to three escalators and a lift up to the southern ticket hall on Kraus torg (1987).

Danderyds sjukhus.note: An island platform 180 m long in a concrete box just under the ground (OpenStreetMap's indoor ways, mapped from SL's plans; Lantmäteriet's laser scan). From its northern end an escalator and stairs, and a lift, climb 4.5 m to the northern ticket hall, which opens onto the sunken walkway beside it to the east, open to the south and climbing north by stairs to the street, a cycle path ramping up beside it; from the hall a passage runs north-west under the hospital's grounds to an escalator and stairs up under the canopy at the hospital's main entrance. From its southern end stairs, and a lift, climb to the southern ticket hall, from which passages run under the bus street to stairs up into the bus terminal's waiting hall, and to stairs and a lift up to the bus stops along its western side.

Mörby centrum.note: The line's northern end: an island platform 24 m wide in a cave 23 m under Mörbyplan, round two cores of rock, a passage between them a little south of the platform's middle (Albert Guillaumes' drawing; OpenStreetMap's indoor ways). From a notch in the southern core's end by the passage four escalators and an inclined lift climb 23.6 m to the south-west, over the western track, to the ticket hall on the ground floor of the shopping centre, from which a passage through the centre leads out to Mörbyplan.

Midsommarkransen.note: Two straight platform halls, one for each track, the tracks on the outside and the side platforms within, either side of a core of rock about 17 m wide, joined through it by a hall a little north-east of the middle (Albert Guillaumes's drawing; OpenStreetMap's platforms). From the hall's north-eastern side three escalators climb north-east inside the core to a passage 12 m up, beside them a corridor to a lift and to the south-eastern platform; past the gates the passage splits: north-west a long walkway rises gently under the hill and Tegelbruksvägen to a door at the hill's foot, and south-east a passage crosses over the south-eastern hall to stairs up into the building on Svandammsvägen, coming out between its shops (OpenStreetMap's indoor ways, 2026, with the escalators, lift and stairs; the passage's height from the escalators' length, the exits' from the ground).

Telefonplan.note: An island platform in a cutting through the rock, narrowing to the east, under a low roof over its western half. From the middle of its western half a ramp climbs along the island to a deck at its west end, where an escalator, stairs and a lift come up beside it from the platform's end; from the deck a ramp goes up into the station's building over the tracks' tunnels, its hall at the street, with doors to the square to the west and to Mikrofonvägen to the south. Laid out from OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping, Lantmäteriet's laser scan and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Hägerstensåsen.note: An island platform in the open between two tracks, its west end on the bridge over Personnevägen, its east end against the station's building over the mouth of the tunnel to Telefonplan. From the west end a stair house between the tracks leads to an escalator and stairs down west to the ticket hall under the bridge, at the street, and a lift beyond them; its doors are in its west front. From the east end a lobby leads to stairs and an escalator up east to the pavilion over the tracks, its doors east onto Sedelvägen, and a glazed lift beside it. Laid out from OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the escalator from 59.6 m to 67.7 m west, the gates at 76 m, the doors at 80 m; the stairs and escalator from 102.4 m east, the gates at 119.5 m, the doors at 129 m), Lantmäteriet's laser scan (the street 5 m under the platform at the west end, the square 5.8 m over it at the east end) and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Västertorp.note: An island platform in the open on the bank between two bridges, over Västertorpsvägen at its south-west end and Störtloppsvägen at its north-east end. From the south-west end stairs and a lift go down in a stair house between the tracks to the ticket hall under the northern track, at the street, its doors south-west to the path to Västertorpsvägen. From the north-east end a ramp goes down between the tracks under a sawtooth of glazed roofs to the ticket hall under the bridge, its doors north-east onto Störtloppsvägen; a path beside the ramp leads to a lift down to the hall. Laid out from OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the stairs from 76 m to 87 m south-west, the lift at 85.7 m; the ramp from 70 m to 126 m north-east, the hall at 129 m, the doors at 139 m), Lantmäteriet's laser scan (the streets 4.8 m and 5.5 m under the platform, the ramp's roofs) and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Fruängen.note: The end of T14, the metro's highest station: an island platform on a bank over the bus terminal, its tracks ending at buffer stops beside the ticket hall at its south end. From the hall a door opens onto the passage to Fruängstorget, and stairs, an escalator and a lift go down to the doors under Fruängens centrum on Fruängsplan.

Aspudden.note: Two straight platform halls, one for each track, the tracks on the outside and the side platforms within, either side of a core of rock about 16.5 m wide, joined through it by a hall 12 m wide a little west of the middle (Albert Guillaumes's drawing; OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping, 2025, which has the platforms' inner edges, the escalators and the passages). From the hall's west side four escalators climb west inside the core to the ticket hall 12 m up, the gates across it; from its west end stairs climb into the glass pavilion on Schlytersvägen, at the corner of Erik Segersälls väg, and a corridor beside them leads to the lift up to the street beside it. A second lift goes down from the ticket hall to the southern platform (OpenStreetMap's lifts and gates; the halls' heights from the street's, Lantmäteriet's laser scan, and the escalators' length).

Örnsberg.note: An island platform in the open, in a cutting between a rock face on the north and a bank up to Hägerstensvägen on the south, roofed at its east end. At that end it runs on under Örnsbergsvägen into a passage between the two tracks' tunnels, and at the passage's end stairs, an escalator and a lift climb into the station building on the street's east side, its ticket hall at the street, its doors east onto the square by Örnsbergsvägen. Laid out from OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the passage from the platform's end to 91 m, the escalator and the stairs to 104 m, the gates at 107.6 m, the doors at 117 m), Lantmäteriet's laser scan (the street 4.1 m over the platform) and photographs of the station.

Axelsberg.note: An island platform in a cutting through the rock, roofed over its eastern two thirds. From the middle of the roofed part a ramp climbs east along the island between walls of clinker, with stairs beside it on the north and a lift at its top on the south, into the ticket hall on the deck over the tracks' east end; the hall rises on to the gates and the doors in the station building's east front, onto the footbridge between Selmedalsvägen and Axelsbergs torg. Laid out from OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the ramp from 53 m to 77.7 m, the stairs beside it, the lift at 78 m, the gates at 94.7 m, the doors at 100.8 m), Lantmäteriet's laser scan (the deck 3.4 m over the platform) and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Mälarhöjden.note: Two straight platform halls, one for each track, the tracks on the outside and the side platforms within, either side of a core of rock 8.7 m wide, joined round its north-east end and by a passage about 62 m from its south-west end (Albert Guillaumes's drawing). From each platform's north-east end a corridor leads on to a passage across, and from its middle a passage runs on north-east to three escalators and an inclined lift, which climb 10 m inside the hill under Mälarhöjdens kyrka to the ticket hall, the gates across it, and the doors in the low front at the hill's foot, onto the square at Slättgårdsvägen and Hägerstensvägen. Laid out from OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the corridors, the passage across at 85 m, the escalators' tops at 130 m, the validator at 138 m, the doors at 160 m), Lantmäteriet's laser scan (the street 10 m over the platform) and photographs of the station. OpenStreetMap's escalators are 38 m long, more than a climb of 10 m needs, so here they start from a level passage.

Bredäng.note: A long island platform on a viaduct over Bredängs Allé, the bus street, the station's base building and Bredängstorget, widening eastwards as its tracks splay apart; its narrow west tip is on the embankment. At its east end, between the tracks and at the platform's level, the ticket hall: a glass wall across the platform, the gates (OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping: the hall's wall 11 m east of the station's node, the validator 18 m), and beyond them a well with an escalator and stairs down eastwards to a lobby on the square, under a deck at the platform's level, its doors in the base building's east face (OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping: the escalator's top 26 m east of the node, the doors 40 m). A walk along the south side of the well leads out onto that deck, and from its east tip a walkway runs east between the tracks, over the square on a deck of its own and on along the ground to Gröna Stugans stig (its heights from Lantmäteriet's laser scan). The lift down to the square, in a round tower beside the well, isn't drawn as a lift.

Sätra.note: Two island platforms in a cutting, the turnback track between them, where no train stops. Sätra centrum stands across the tracks at their south ends, and each island runs into a stair house of its own under the centre's north front: a ramp climbs to it from the island's middle in a long tiled house on the platform, beside a passage to the lift, and stairs climb beside them, to a landing over the platforms' ends at the centre's floor. A crossing over the turnback track joins the two landings, and from the gates in the centre's north wall the way out is through its indoor square, west to its doors onto Sätratorget or east to those towards Torvsätravägen. From the laser scan (the platforms 148 m long, the ramp houses from 49 m to 74 m south of their middle, their roofs climbing from 4 m to 6.4 m over the platforms, the stair houses on to 88 m, the centre's floor 3.85 m over the platforms), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the stairs, lifts and ramps, the gates at 97 m, the doors) and photographs (2005 to 2024).

Skärholmen.note: An island platform in a concrete box just under Skärholmsterrassen (OpenStreetMap's indoor ways; Lantmäteriet's laser scan for the street and the terrace). In its middle two flights, each an escalator and stairs, climb towards each other from the platform to the ticket hall at the street's level, 4.3 m over it, a lift between their heads; past the gates the hall opens south onto Skärholmsgången, under the terrace's front. From the platform's east end a passage runs on 46 m between the tracks to an escalator, stairs and an inclined lift up to the eastern ticket hall, which opens south onto Skärholmsgången at the bus terminal. (OpenStreetMap draws the passage across the southern track, as mapped; it is laid between the tracks here.)

Vårberg.note: An island platform in the open, in a shallow cutting, narrowing eastwards, under a butterfly roof over its western part. The tracks run on into Vårberg centrum, the shopping centre built over them at the platform's west end, and the station's building stands between them against its east wall. From the platform's middle a ramp climbs in a long tiled house to the ticket hall in the centre's ground floor, level with its indoor square; beside the ramp's head stairs climb from the platform's end, and a lift beside the northern stairs. Past the gates the hall's doors open onto the centre's shopping street, which runs south to a footbridge over Vårbergsplan. From the laser scan (the platform 145 m long, the roof from its west end 97 m east, 3.3 m over the platform in its middle and 3.7 m at its edges, the ramp's house 5.3 m high, 6.6 m nearer the centre, the hall 3.95 m over the platform), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the ramp, the stairs, the lift, the gates, the hall's doors, the shopping street and the footbridge) and photographs (2006 to 2020).

Vårby gård.note: An island platform on a bank over the square to the south-west, its north-western end on the abutment of the line's viaducts, under a flat roof from the ticket hall at its south-eastern end 101 m north-west. The hall stands on the platform between the tracks; past its gates its doors open onto the platform's end beyond it, out in the open in the cutting, where a ramp climbs south-east beside the southern track to Vårby allé, stairs climb to the deck over the northern track, stairs and an escalator under the deck lead down to a passage under the southern track out to the square, and a lift joins the three levels. From the laser scan (the platform 144 m long, the roof 3.2 to 3.5 m over it, the hall 3.4 m, the deck 3.6 m over the end and the square 5.4 to 6.7 m under the retaining wall), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the gates, the doors, the stairs, the escalator, the lift, the passage under the tracks, the ramp) and photographs (2006 to 2024).

Masmo.note: An island platform in a cave under Masmoberget, near the foot of its rock face. A stair climbs from the middle of the platform to the ticket hall over it, a lift beside it. From the hall's gates a passage runs back west-south-west, over the cave's northern side, to the entrance in the rock face on the square, under a canopy that Lantmäteriet's laser scan places.

Fittja.note: An island platform on grade, under a flat roof on pairs of posts. At its north-eastern end a glazed screen closes it off from the way on under the footbridge to the foot of a stair, an inclined lift and an escalator side by side, which climb north-east to the ticket hall over the southern track. Past the hall's gates its doors open north-east onto the walkway in front of it, on the deck over the tracks, where the buses stop, and Fittja centrum. From the laser scan (the platform's surface 19.72-19.83 m, the roof 3.4 m over it, the hall's floor and the deck 4.05 m), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the passage, the stair, the escalator, the lift, the gates, the doors and the hall's outline) and photographs (2018), which show the lift's doors at the stair's foot and at its head.

Alby.note: Three tracks in a cave under Albyberget: an island platform between the northern track and the middle one, where trains ending at Alby stand, and a side platform for the southern track beyond a wall of rock. From the platforms' eastern ends a stair each climbs east to the ticket hall over the tracks, a lift beside each on its north side. Past the gates a corridor runs north and south: south to the entrance from Alby centrum's square, north to the foot of three long escalators and an inclined lift up to the entrance on Albyberget, at Tingstorget. From OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the stairs, the lifts, the gates, the corridor, the escalators and the entrances), Albert Guillaumes's drawing (2024) and photographs (2002 to 2018); the hall's height (one level up, at the square's) is a guess, and the escalators are drawn at their usual slope, 12 m further along than OpenStreetMap's feet.

Hallunda.note: An island platform in the open, on a shelf at the northern foot of the hill of Eriksberg, under one long flat roof; the tracks part eastwards, so the platform widens from 8 m at its western end to 16 m at its eastern. At its eastern end a glazed vestibule over the heads of an escalator and a stair down east, 5.5 m, to the ticket hall between the tracks, and a lift beside it. Past the hall's gates its doors open onto a high passage under a skylight: north from it a covered footbridge runs under the northern track and over Hallundavägen to the bus station at Hallunda centrum, where an escalator and stairs go down west to the street and a lift beside them; south a passage runs under the southern track to three escalators and an inclined lift up the hill to the entrance on Skarpbrunnavägen. From OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the escalator, the stair, the lifts, the gates, the passages, the footbridge, the escalators and the entrances), Lantmäteriet's laser scan (the platform, the roof, the hall's roof at 33.0 m, the footbridge's at 30.6–30.9 m, the ground beside the line) and photographs (2006, 2018). The hall's floor, at the ground north of the line, is a guess, and the escalators up the hill are drawn at their usual slope, which puts their feet 10 m south of OpenStreetMap's.

Norsborg.note: The end of the red line's Norsborg branch: an island platform in the open, on a shelf at the northern foot of the hill of Eriksberg, under one long butterfly roof on orange steel. A rock face rises south of the southern track. At the platform's eastern end a glazed vestibule over the heads of an escalator and a stair down east, 4 m, to the ticket hall under the tracks, and a lift beside them. Past the hall's gates, doors open onto a lobby under a glazed lantern: north from it a stair and a lift go down under the northern track to the bus station at Norsborgs centrum; south a passage runs under the southern track to three escalators and an inclined lift up the hill to the entrance on Skarpbrunnavägen. From OpenStreetMap (the gates, the entrances, the escalators up the hill), Lantmäteriet's laser scan (the platform, 146 m long at 31.73 m, the roof, the hall's roof at 32.6 m and the lantern's at 35.4 m, the ground beside the line) and photographs (2006, 2018, 2023). The hall's floor is a guess, from the stair's risers and the headroom under the tracks.

Hötorget.note: An island platform deep under Sveavägen, with three ticket halls: one over the middle of the platform, under the street at Hötorget, and one at each end.

Rådmansgatan.note: An island platform 150 m long under Sveavägen (1952), one row of yellow-tiled columns down its middle. From its south end escalators climb 4.3 m to the southern ticket hall under the street, a lift beside them; through the gates passages lead west under the crossing with Rådmansgatan, past Sture V Nilsson's Strindberg wall (1983), to stairs up into the ground floor of the corner building, and east to stairs up into the glass pavilion on the eastern pavement, and a lift climbs to its tower on the western pavement. From its north end escalators climb 5.6 m to the northern ticket hall, an inclined lift beside them (the lift itself isn't walked); through the gates passages lead north-west to stairs up into the small glazed house at the park's corner, a lift beside them climbing to its tower, and north-east under the crossing with Rehnsgatan to stairs up into the ground floor of the corner building, Sveavägen 98. From OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the flights, lifts, halls and passages), the elevation model (the street 7.2 to 7.4 m above the platform at the south end, 8.5 to 9.1 m at the north end), Google's 3D mesh (the pavilion, the house's shape and the lift towers, the southern one 3.6 m south of OpenStreetMap's lift) and photographs (1955, 2005–2023); the halls' columns and booth are placed from photographs, and the pavilion's doors are inferred.

Sankt Eriksplan.note: An island platform 154 m long under Sankt Eriksgatan (1952), on two rows of columns in exposed-aggregate concrete. From its south end an escalator and stairs climb 3.8 m to the southern ticket hall under the square, a lift beside them; through the gates a passage leads south-west to stairs up into the glazed stair house on the square's western side, a lift beside it climbing to its tower, and another south-east to the glass pavilion, whose escalator and stairs climb to its doors at its south end and whose lift climbs inside it, and on under the square, falling 1 m, to stairs up through the pavement on its south-eastern side. From its north end an escalator and stairs climb 4.6 m to the northern ticket hall, an inclined lift beside them (the lift itself isn't walked); through the gates a few steps climb to the stairs up into the barrel-roofed stair house at the corner of Torsgatan, a lift beside it climbing to its glazed tower. From OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the flights, lifts, halls and passages; its moving walkway at the north end is drawn as an escalator, and the steps beyond the northern gates turned to climb along the hall), the elevation model (the street 6.6 m above the platform round the square, 5.6 m at the south-eastern stairs and 10.2 m at the north end), the laser scan and Google's 3D mesh (the stair houses, the pavilion and the lift towers) and photographs (2008–2023); the halls' heights are inferred from the flights' lengths.

Thorildsplan.note: An island platform in the open between the carriageways of Drottningholmsvägen, under a roof of fourteen vaulted bays on blue steel from 4.5 m to 88.5 m east of its middle. A ramp goes down the middle of its eastern half, open between tiled parapets from 30 m to 64 m and then under the platform's end and a walkway, to the ticket hall between the tracks; beside it, from the platform's end, a flight of stairs down on either side, and between them the walkway out to a lift. From the gates a passage runs north under the tracks and the road to stairs and a lift up by a glass pavilion at the street, and south under the tracks and the motorway ramp to a portal in a sunken court, with stairs up the slope. From OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the flights from 76 m to 86 m, the walkway and its lift at 88 m, the gates at 100 m, the passage at 108 m, the pavilion's stairs and the lift beside them), Albert Guillaumes' drawing (the ramp's opening from about 30 m to 64 m), the laser scan (the roof's top 4.1 m to 5 m over the platform, the court 3.6 m under it) and photographs (2009 to 2025). The hall lies 4.6 m under the platform rather than about 4 m, so that the passage fits under the network's tracks, which run lower here than the scan's.

Kristineberg.note: An island platform on a bank, entered only from its west end. There a stair house stands between the tracks: a flight down along its middle to the ticket hall at the street, and a glazed walkway along the northern track to a lift. West of it the tracks run on concrete decks over the hall, which lies under the northern one and between them, and over Nordenflychtsvägen, which passes under the tracks and Drottningholmsvägen. From the gates the way out is north through the hall's doors onto Nordenflychtsvägen, where Hjalmar Söderbergs väg meets it. From the laser scan (the stair house, its roof sloping down from the platform, the lift's tower, the decks, the streets 5.3 m under the platform), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the flight's foot 90 m west, the lift at 93 m, the gates and the doors at 91.5 m) and photographs (2010 to 2019).

Alvik.note: Two island platforms on a bank, the metro along their outer edges and the Nockebybanan's tram tracks between them, ending at buffers where the islands join at the east end. At the west end, from each island an escalator and stairs go down under a glazed roof to the ticket hall under the bank at Alviks torg, and a glazed walkway along the tram tracks leads to a lift; the hall's doors face west under the trams' bridge. At the east end an escalator and stairs climb from the junction to a footbridge over the northern track, and from its north end a passage goes into the hillside, where escalators and a lift climb to the pavilion on Tranebergsvägen; a lift from the junction reaches the footbridge too. From the laser scan (the platforms, the stair houses' roofs, the trams' bridge, the footbridge 4.1 m and the pavilion 8 m over the platform), OpenStreetMap (the buildings, the entrances) and photographs.

Stora mossen.note: An island platform on the bank beside Drottningholmsvägen, under a roof over its eastern part. At its east end the platform runs into the station's hall between the tracks: the ticket gates, then stairs down along its south side and a walkway along its north side to a lift, both to the passage under the tracks, which comes out towards Drottningholmsvägen to the north and onto Stora Mossens backe to the south. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Abrahamsberg.note: An island platform in a cutting, under a roof over all but its eastern end. West of the platform's end, between the tracks, stands a glazed hall: straight stairs go down westwards along its south side, and a walkway along its north side leads to a lift; both reach a passage that runs west, then south under the southern track, to the ticket hall in the street south of the tracks, whose doors open onto the square by Abrahamsbergsvägen. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing has a ramp down to the south where there are stairs down to the west.

Brommaplan.note: An island platform on a bank, under a roof over its western half. At its west end stands a low enclosure over the way down: an escalator with a stair beside it go down westwards under the platform, and a walkway along their south side leads to a lift at the end. At their foot a corridor goes on west into the ticket hall, which stands on the square under the tracks' two decks, under a glass vault between them; its doors open west onto Tunnlandet. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing has the stairs going down to the south-west under the southern track, where they go down to the west under the platform.

Åkeshov.note: Two island platforms on a low bank between Bergslagsvägen and Åkeshov's park, the track where the T17 turns between them, each under a butterfly roof of its own over its eastern part. At each island's east end a glazed housing stands between the tracks: a stair down eastwards with a landing halfway, and a walkway beside it to a lift in a glass tower. They come down into the ticket hall under the tracks' decks, the sculpture between the stairs' feet and one line of gates; its glass front opens east onto the footway and cycleway under the line. From there the way out is south at grade onto the forecourt towards Åkeshovs slott, north up a stair in a trough beside the tracks to Bergslagsvägen's service road, or north through the tunnel under Bergslagsvägen to the small entrance building beyond it. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan (the housings, the lift towers, the hall's roofs between the decks, the forecourt 5.3 m under the platform), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the stairs, walkways, lifts, gates, the underpass and the tunnel) and photographs (1954 to 2026); Albert Guillaumes' drawing has the stairs from the middle of the platforms to a passage at s 62, with gates at each exit.

Ängbyplan.note: An island platform on the bank, under a butterfly roof over its west half. At its west end a glazed hall between the tracks at the platform's level, with the ticket gates and a lift; beyond it a glass stair house over two flights of stairs down into a trough between the bridges' abutments, out under the bridges onto Färjestadsvägen's pavement. The lift goes down to a passage under the southern track, out onto a forecourt beside the street. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan (the roof, the stair house's roof falling from 3.1 m over the platform to 0.9 m, the street 5.8 m under it), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the gates, the lift, the stair) and photographs (2006 to 2024); Albert Guillaumes' drawing has stairs from the middle of the platform down to a hall at the street with its exit to the north.

Islandstorget.note: An island platform at grade, under a butterfly roof over its west and middle parts, the east end open. At its west end, over the mouths of the tunnels on to Blackeberg, a single-storey ticket hall at the street's level, glazed towards Blackebergsvägen, with the ticket gates; beyond them a housing with a sloping roof over the stairs down to the platform in three short flights. A lift tower stands on the platform east of the housing, reached from the hall by an enclosed gallery along the platform's south side. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan (the street and the hall's floor 3.4 m over the platform, the housing's roof falling from 6.4 m to 3.3 m, the gallery's 6.3 m, the lift tower's 7.3 m), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the gates, the stair, the gallery, the lift) and photographs (1944 to 2025); Albert Guillaumes' drawing has the station in a cutting, a stair rising 4.8 m from the middle of the platform, no lift, and the exit 28 m north of the real door.

Blackeberg.note: An island platform, its south-eastern part covered under Vinjegatan's deck, the ticket hall and Blackebergs torg, its north-western part open in a rock cutting. The ticket hall spans the tracks at Vinjegatan's level, 4.1 m over the platform: from the gates, stairs go down to the platform, with a landing under the shops, and a lift beside them; from the hall, two doors lead through to Vinjegatan, a double stair along the front wall climbs to the doors on Blackebergs torg, and a lift in the north-eastern wall rises to the square. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan (the street and the hall's floor 4.1 m over the platform, the square 7.7 m), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the gates, the stairs, both lifts, the doors) and photographs (1950s to 2019); Albert Guillaumes' drawing has the hall's floor at the square's level, 7.6 m up one flight from the platform.

Råcksta.note: An island platform in the open on a bank, on a curve, the viaduct over Bergslagsvägen at its south end and the bridge over Jämtlandsgatan at its north. At the north end the stairs go down between the tracks, in three flights under a sloping glazed housing, to the passage under the eastern track and the ticket hall on Råcksta torg at Jämtlandsgatan's level, 6.45 m below the platform; a walkway along the housing's west side leads to the lift down to the passage. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan (the street and the hall's floor 6.45 m below the platform, the housing's roof falling from 2.85 m to 0.4 m), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the stairs, the lift, the gates, the hall's outline and entrance) and photographs (2006 to 2018); Albert Guillaumes' drawing has the stairs from the middle of the platform and the hall under the tracks.

Vällingby.note: Two island platforms 143 m long, with the turnback track between them, where no train stops, and the outer tracks beyond them. Their south-eastern 100 m are covered, under Kirunaplan's bus terminal on its deck and the car park's deck north-west of it; the rest is in the open under two butterfly roofs. At the south-eastern end escalators, stairs and a lift climb from each island to the ticket hall under Vällingby centrum, 4.67 m above the platforms, with exits onto Kirunaplan, Vällingby torg and the streets either side; at the north-western end stairs in glazed houses, and a lift beside each, go down from each island to the hall under the tracks by Bräckegatan, 4.6 m below the platforms. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan (the decks 4.4 to 5.3 m over the platforms, the street under the bridge 4.5 m below them), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the stairs, escalators, lifts and gates at both ends, the entrances) and photographs (2006 to 2026).

Johannelund.note: Two side platforms on a bank, a butterfly roof over the middle of each. From the back of each, stairs go down eastwards in an open well to a passage under the tracks; the ticket hall is at its north end, its doors out to the forecourt on the north side. A lift beside each roof's east end. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan (the forecourt 5.2 m below the platforms, the roofs), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the stairs, the lifts, the passage, the gates and the doors) and photographs (2006 to 2023); Albert Guillaumes' drawing has the stairs from the middle of the platforms and the way out to the north, as here.

Hässelby gård.note: An island platform on a viaduct over Hässelby torg, a butterfly roof over its middle. Two openings through the platform's west end go down to the ticket hall under the tracks, at the square's level: the long one with an escalator and stairs, the short one at the very end with the lift's tower. The hall faces the square westwards, its gates beside the lift. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan (the square 7.9 m under the platform, the roof, the openings and the lift's tower), OpenStreetMap (the way in) and photographs (2006 to 2018); Albert Guillaumes' drawing has the two openings, the escalator beside the stairs, the lift between them and the way out to the west, as here.

Hässelby strand.note: The western end of the line: a wide island platform in the open under a butterfly roof. Down its middle a box walls in a ramp, which runs straight down at 1 in 12 past the end of the roof, under a low box over the platform's south end and into a hall under a sloping roof, 5.07 m down; from the box a lift and stairs go down into the same hall. Through the ground floor of the 2015 building on Fyrspannsgatan the ticket hall, its gates and its glass front on the street. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan (the roof, the box and the lift's shaft over it, the hall's roof, the street 5.05 m under the platform), OpenStreetMap (the building and the way in) and photographs (2009 to 2023); Albert Guillaumes' drawing has the ramp down from the platform's middle, the lift's tower at its end, the stairs beside it and the gates by the way out, as here.

Medborgarplatsen.note: An island platform 145 m long in the concrete box of the 1933 tram tunnel under Götgatan, its northern third the vaulted lengthening of 1950. From its south end an escalator and stairs side by side climb 4.1 m to the ticket hall under the crossing with Folkungagatan; through the gates passages lead east and west under the street to stairs up into the ground floors of the corner buildings, the hotel at Folkungagatan 47 and Medborgarhuset at 45, the western one curving past Mari Pårup's mosaics (1997). Near the middle of the platform an escalator climbs north and stairs climb south to a landing under the street, a lift beside them; from it an escalator and stairs, a lift beside them, climb 3.9 m into the glass pavilion in Björns trädgård (1995), its gates just inside its doors. From OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (2025; its platform is drawn in the wrong place, so its flights are set on the real one), the elevation model (the street 7.8 to 8.0 m above the platform at the three entrances) and photographs (2009–2025); the landing's layout is inferred.

Skanstull.note: An island platform 180 m long in the concrete box of the old tram tunnel under Götgatan (1933, lengthened for the metro in 1950). At its south end an escalator and stairs side by side, and a lift beside them, climb 3.55 m to a low ticket hall under the street, just above the trains; through the gates a lift rises to Götgatan's median, a passage leads east over the northbound track and down a few steps into a sunken court with stairs up to the pavement at each end, one of them in a glass stair house with a lift beside it, and a passage leads south-west under the building on the corner and Ringvägen to a glass stair house on Ringvägen's north side and to open stairs at its south-west corner. At the north end stairs lead down under the southbound track to a passage west, and three escalators climb 10.2 m to the hall under the end of Allhelgonagatan, whose glass front, under the street's railing, opens onto Götgatan. From OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the flights, lifts, gates, passages and entrances), the laser scan (the court's floor 2.6 m over the platform and the pavement round it at 4.6 m; Allhelgonagatan's end 3.2 m above Götgatan's pavement; the stair houses' roofs; the open stairs at Ringvägen) and photographs (2013).

Gullmarsplan.note: Two island platforms where the line divides, the southern half of each under the deck that carries Johanneshovsvägen over the tracks and its southern end under the bus terminal beyond it. From the south end of each, stairs and an escalator side by side climb into the terminal, and a lift from its very end; through the gates the way out is north through the terminal's doors onto the square on the deck. From OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the flights from 62 m to 73 m south of the platforms' middle, the lifts at 73 m, the gates at 76 m, the doors at 61 m), the laser scan (the deck and the square, 4.4–5.2 m over the platforms; the terminal from 61 m to 83 m south) and photographs (2008 to 2025).

Skärmarbrink.note: Two island platforms in the open where the Farsta and Skarpnäck branches part. At their south-east ends glass stair houses climb from each platform to the ticket hall on its bridge over the tracks, and a lift from each; from the gates the way out is through the hall's doors onto the footbridge in front of it, south-west to Pelargatan or north-east over Palandergatan. From the laser scan (the hall from 65 m to 74 m south-east of the platforms' middle, its floor and the footbridge's 4.7 m over the platforms, the footbridge rising to 5.05 m at its south-western end and falling to 4.36 m at its north-eastern), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the flights from 56 m to 65 m, the lifts at 68 m and 70 m, the gates at 72 m) and photographs (2008 to 2025).

Hammarbyhöjden.note: An island platform in the open (1958, rebuilt 2003), with a ticket hall at each end. At the west end, a stair house beyond the platform's end between the tracks: the stairs go down its north half, and a corridor along its south half leads to the lift, to the ticket hall under the tracks; from the gates the way out is through the hall's glass front onto the underpass, up a few steps to Finn Malmgrens plan or on to Tidaholmsplan. At the east end, a walkway between the tracks goes down to a glass house between the bridges, and the stairs and a lift in a brick tower go down to the hall at the street, its door onto Ulricehamnsvägen. From the laser scan (the west stair house's roof 3 m over the platform from 73.4 m to 89.5 m west, the walkway 2 m down at 132 m east, the street 8.5 m under the platform at the hall's door), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the gates at 98 m west, the lifts at 83 m west and 145 m east, the east flights and the door) and photographs (2009 to 2025).

Björkhagen.note: An island platform on a bank (1958), with a glass hall on the platform in its middle. From the glass hall an escalator and stairs go down a long well to the ticket hall under the platform's northern part, and a lift runs down to it from the platform beyond the glass hall; from the gates the way out is through the hall's glass front onto the underpass under the tracks, west to Falsterbovägen and east to Malmövägen. From OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the glass hall's doors 17 m south of the platform's middle, the escalator and stairs from 5.4 m to 22.6 m north, the lift at 28.7 m, the gates at 30.5 m, the hall's door at 38.2 m), the laser scan (the ground at the underpass 4.9 m under the platform) and photographs (2008 to 2026).

Kärrtorp.note: An island platform in the open, beside Kärrtorps centrum. At its south end a glazed stair house stands between the tracks: two escalators and stairs go down it to the ticket hall at the street, under and between the tracks' two bridges, and a corridor along its east side leads to the lift. From the gates the way out is through the hall's doors onto Kärrtorpsplan. From the laser scan (the stair house from 73 m to 90 m south of the platform's middle, the lift's tower at 94 m, the street 6.3 m under the platform) and photographs (2007 to 2021).

Bagarmossen.note: An island platform in the rock, 19 m down. From a lobby at its north end three escalators climb 32 m to the ticket hall in the pavilion on Bagarmossen's square, an inclined lift beside them (its car at the lobby; the lift itself isn't walked); from the gates the way out is through the doors at the pavilion's point. From OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the escalators and the lift climbing from the platform's north end, the ticket validators at the tall part's front), the laser scan (the street 18.6 m over the platform, the pavilion's axis 9° from the platform's) and photographs (2014 to 2022).

Skarpnäck.note: The end of the green line: an island platform in a cave 25 m down, the tracks running on past its south end to buffers. At its north end stairs, an escalator and a lift climb 4.4 m to a landing over the platform; from it a passage leads west into the rock to the foot of three long escalators, an inclined lift beside them, which climb 20.5 m to the ticket hall in the brick station building on Skarpnäcks allé; from the gates the way out is through its glass front under the deep canopy. From OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the short flights and the lift at the platform's north end, the passage, the long escalators and the inclined lift, the building and its door), the laser scan (the street 24.9 m over the platform, the building's two parts and its clerestory) and photographs (2008 to 2022).

Blåsut.note: An island platform on the bank, under a butterfly roof over its southern half. At its south end the platform runs into the station's hall between the tracks, over the cycle path's underpass: the ticket gates, then stairs down along its east side and a walkway along its west side to a glass lift, both to the underpass, which comes out towards Blåsutvägen to the west and Fyrvaktarkroken to the east. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Sandsborg.note: An island platform on the bank, under a flat red steel roof over its southern half. At its south end the platform runs into the station's hall between the tracks, over the underpass of Stora Gungans väg: the ticket gates, then stairs down along its west side and a walkway along its east side to a lift, both to the underpass, which comes out on Stora Gungans väg to the west and towards Dalens allé to the east. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Skogskyrkogården.note: An island platform in the open, by the cemetery, its north end on the tracks' bridges over Sockenvägen. There the platform runs on into a glass building between the bridges: a walkway at the platform's level on its west side out to a lift, and stairs down on its east side, both to the ticket hall at the street, with the gates and the door towards Sockenvägen. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Tallkrogen.note: An island platform on the bank, under a butterfly roof over its south half, which also covers a narrow hall on the platform with the ticket gates and a lift. Beyond the hall a glass stair house between the tracks, with two flights of stairs down to the door onto Victor Balcks väg under the tracks' bridges; the lift goes down to a passage under the western track out to Tallkrogsvägen. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping and photographs of the station.

Gubbängen.note: An island platform at ground level on the hillside, under a long butterfly roof, the track on a low bank. At its south end a short hall with the ticket gates, then stairs down southwards to a passage under the tracks, with a way out on each side. At its north end a glass stair house, with an escalator and stairs up to the ticket hall on the Herrhagsvägen bridge, which opens onto the street to the east. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, Google's 3D mesh and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Hökarängen.note: An island platform out in the open on a long curve, under a butterfly roof. At its south end a glass hall with the ticket gates, then stairs down to a passage under the tracks, with a way out on each side. At its north end the platform runs on, narrowing, into a glass stair house, with an escalator and stairs down to the ticket hall under the track's bridge, which opens towards Örbyleden. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Farsta.note: An island platform on the viaduct over Munkforsplan and Kroppaplan, under a long W-shaped roof. Two glass halls on the platform each stand over an escalator and a wide stair down towards the middle, to the ticket hall under the tracks; between them a lift. The ticket gates are in the hall's west wall, and beyond them a passage runs west between shops through the building on Farsta torg, with a way out to Kroppaplan on its north side; to the east a short way out under the viaduct comes out on Larsbodavägen. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, OpenStreetMap and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Farsta strand.note: The end of T18: an island platform in a long, low box under Centrumhuset and Stieg Trenters torg, where the line once ran in an open cutting. In the middle two flights, each stairs beside an escalator, climb towards each other to the ticket hall in the pavilion on the square, with a lift between them; the ticket gates are on the hall's east side, and the way out is on the square, by the kiosk. Laid out from OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping, Lantmäteriet's laser scan and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Globen.note: An island platform in a cutting between Palmfeltsvägen and the tram's platform, under a long butterfly roof that widens with the platform towards its east end. At the east end escalators and stairs climb in a glazed house to the ticket hall on Globenbron, its gates in the middle, and out onto the bridge; at the west end stairs climb in a glazed tube to a small hall on Slakthusbron, its gates at the top. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, OpenStreetMap and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Enskede gård.note: An island platform on the bank, under a butterfly roof. At its north end the platform runs on into a glass stair house between the tracks: a walkway at the platform's level along its west side out to a lift, and stairs down along its east side, both to the ticket hall in the bank, with the gates, and on into the footway's underpass under the tracks, which comes out towards Odelbergsvägen to the west and Palmfeltsvägen to the east. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Sockenplan.note: An island platform on the bank, curving towards its south end. At its north end it runs into a glass stair house between the tracks, where they go onto their bridges over the square: a walkway on the platform's level out to a lift on its west side, stairs down on its east, both to the ticket hall under the bridges at the street, its doors to the north. From the laser scan (the house from 73.5 m to 91 m north, the hall's roof between the bridges to 101 m, the street 5 m under the platform), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the stairs from 76 m to 89 m, the lift at 88 m, the gates at 93 m) and photographs (2018).

Svedmyra.note: An island platform on a bank at its south end and on a concrete viaduct from its middle north, over the square and the street. Two long flights of stairs go down from the platform, one from its south half and one from under the roof's north end, and a lift from its middle, to the ticket hall under the viaduct at the street; from its gates a passage runs east under the tracks to the low entrance building at the foot of the bank, its doors under a curved canopy onto the square. From the laser scan (the street 6.1 m under the platform, the lift's head through the roof 13 m north, the entrance building's roof), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the flights from 14 m south down to the hall and from 38 m north down to 25 m, the lift at 14 m, the gates at 7 m) and photographs (2009 to 2024).

Stureby.note: An island platform on a low bank, entered only from its west end. There a glass stair house stands on the platform: a flight down along its south side and a lift at its west end, to the ticket hall under the concrete deck that carries the tracks west of the platform, between them at the street. From the gates the way out is through the hall's west doors into the footway under the deck, out to Munksjövägen on the south and Sågverksgatan on the north. From the laser scan (the deck's edges and the streets 4.45 m under the platform, the stair house's roof and the lift's tower), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the flight from 75 m to 87 m west, the lift at 86 m, the gates at 98 m, the footway at 114 m) and photographs (2008 to 2018).

Bandhagen.note: An island platform on a bank, its south end on a bridge over Trollesundsvägen, where a glazed hall stands between the tracks' decks: an escalator, and stairs beside it, go down its west side to the ticket hall under it at the street, and a walkway along its east side leads to the lift. From the gates the way out is through the doors in the hall's south front onto Bandhagsplan. From the laser scan (the platform from 76 m south of its middle to 73 m north, the glazed hall's roof from 72 m to 97 m south, the lift's tower at 104 m, the ticket hall's roof from 85 m to 114 m and the street 6.4 m under the platform), Swedish Wikipedia (the entrance from Bandhagsplan) and photographs (2009 to 2018).

Högdalen.note: Two island platforms in a shallow cutting, a middle track to the depot between them that no train stops at. At their south ends each runs into a stair house under the library's building: in the western one stairs and a lift, in the eastern one an escalator, stairs and a lift, up to the ticket hall in the building at the street. From the gates the way out is south through its doors onto Högdalsgången. From the laser scan (the platforms 145 m long, the stair houses' roofs climbing with the stairs from the platforms' roofs to the building, the building from 94 m to 112 m south of the platforms' middle, the street 5.6 m over the platforms), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the flights from 79 m to 92 m south, the gates at 103 m) and photographs (2008 to 2026).

Rågsved.note: An island platform on a bank, its south-western end on a bridge over the passage under the tracks. Under its W-shaped roof a glazed stair house: an escalator, and stairs beside it, go down from its north-eastern door to the ticket hall at the street under the platform, and from the gates the way out is through the doors in the hall's south-western front onto the passage. A lift in a glazed tower at the roof's south-western end goes down to the hall. From the laser scan (the platform from 58 m south-west of its middle to 90 m north-east, the roof from 19 m south-west to 49 m north-east, the passage 6.95 m under the platform), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the flights, the gates at 27 m south-west, the lift at 19 m) and photographs (2008 to 2025).

Hagsätra.note: The end of T19 (1960): a wide island platform out in the open, the tracks on bridges at its south-eastern end. From the roof's south-eastern end a ramp goes down a well in the middle of the platform, and a stair hall beyond it, between two flights of stairs, to the ticket hall under the tracks, where the lift (2011, in place of a moving walkway) comes down in a glass shaft; from the gates the way out is through the hall's glass front onto the passage under the tracks, to Hagsätra torg. From the laser scan (the well from 27.5 m south-east of the platform's middle to 63.5 m, the stair hall's roof falling from 3 m over the platform to the ticket hall's, the passage 4 m under the platform), OpenStreetMap and photographs (2018).

Kungsträdgården.note: The end of the blue line, 34 m down: two platform halls in one great cavern, one for each track, joined at both ends and in the middle. From the west end, escalators climb in two flights to the ticket hall under Jakobsgatan; from the east end, two flights to the hall in Kungsträdgården park.

Rådhuset.note: Two platform halls in the rock under Kungsholmen, one for each track, joined at both ends and in the middle. From the west end, escalators climb in two flights to a ticket hall with exits on Hantverkargatan and Kungsholmsgatan; from the east end, two flights and a long passage to Kungsholmsgatan.

Stadshagen.note: Two platform halls, one for each track, joined at both ends and in the middle. From the south-east end, escalators climb to the ticket hall at Kellgrensgatan and the sports ground; from the north-west end, to Mariedalsvägen.

Västra skogen.note: Where the line splits for Hjulsta and Akalla: three tracks in the rock, the trains into town on the two eastern ones, beside two platform halls joined at both ends and in the middle; the trains out of town on the western track, beside its own platform, reached by stairs and a footbridge over the tracks. From the south end, escalators climb 7 m, then the metro's longest, 66 m and 33 m high, to the one exit.

Huvudsta.note: An island platform in the rock, 25 m down. Escalators climb in two flights from its west end to the ticket hall at Huvudsta centrum.

Solna strand.note: An island platform in the rock, 28 m down. Escalators climb from its north end to the ticket hall at Solna strand.

Sundbybergs centrum.note: An island platform in the rock, 26 m down. From its south end escalators climb to a ticket hall with exits round Sundbyberg's centre; from the north end, to Prästgårdsgatan.

Duvbo.note: An island platform in the rock, 20–35 m down. From its south-east end escalators climb in two flights to the ticket hall at Duvbo.

Rissne.note: Two platforms in the rock, side by side between the tracks, joined along their middle. Escalators climb between them to the ticket hall at Rissne's centre.

Rinkeby.note: Two platforms in the rock, each outside its track, with the link to Rissnedepån between them (not drawn). From the south-east end of each, escalators climb over the tracks to a landing, and on to the ticket hall at Rinkebytorget.

Tensta.note: An island platform in the rock, 20–22 m down. Escalators climb from both ends: to the ticket hall at Tensta centrum in the east, and to Hjulstavägen in the west.

Hjulsta.note: The end of T10: an island platform in the rock under Hjulstaskolan, the tracks running on beyond it. From its south-east end escalators climb to a landing, and a passage leads over the tracks to the ticket hall at Hjulsta torg.

Solna centrum.note: Two platform halls in the rock under Skytteholmsparken, 27–36 m down, one for each track, joined at both ends and in the middle. From the middle, escalators climb south to the ticket hall at Centralvägen and the bus terminal; from the north end, to the hall at the shopping centre.

Näckrosen.note: Two platform halls in the rock under the old film studios, 21 m down, one for each track, joined at both ends and in the middle. Escalators climb from both ends: to Storskogstorget in Sundbyberg in the north, and to Råsundavägen in Solna in the south.

Hallonbergen.note: An island platform in the rock, 28 m down; a third track beside it, which the trains use only to and from Rissnedepån, isn't drawn. From its north-west end escalators climb to the ticket hall at Hallonbergen's centre.

Kista.note: The only station of the blue line in the open (1977): a wide island platform on the viaduct over the bus terminal and Kista Galleria, each track on a deck of its own, under one long flat roof on light-blue steel, open at the sides, with three openings over the platform's middle that Lars Erik Falk's leaning staves rise through. Both ends are glazed ticket halls on the platform: past the north-western one's gates escalators and a stair go down to the footbridge's level, which runs under the tracks to Köpenhamnsgatan, and a stair on down to the bus terminal; past the south-eastern one's, escalators go down into the Galleria, along its indoor street to Kista torg, or on down to Vejlegatan. From OpenStreetMap (the platform, the gates, the escalators, the entrances), Lantmäteriet's laser scan (the platform at 25.5 m, the roof at 29.35 m, the decks, the footbridge, the streets and the square) and photographs (2001 to 2026). The levels under the platform are guesses from the footbridge's deck and the square.

Husby.note: An island platform in the rock under Husby centrum. Escalators climb in two flights from both ends, to the ticket halls at Trondheimsgatan in the south and Bergengatan in the north.

Akalla.note: The end of T11: two platform halls in the rock, 20 m down, one for each track, joined at both ends and in the middle. From the north-west end, escalators climb to the ticket hall at Akalla torg and its underground bus terminal; from the south-east end, to Sibeliusgången.
